Morning Brief: Operational progress across Bihar power utilities remains active with consumer smart prepaid meter deployments reaching 9.72 million (55.6% coverage) and MKVSY Phase-I exceeding targets at 109,844 agricultural connections. However, critical capital flows remain constrained with over ₹795 Cr in RDSS Phase-IV subsidy claims pending REC approval subject to quantity variation clearances, alongside statutory wildlife clearances stalling off-grid connections in tiger reserve and forest corridors. Clean energy initiatives show strong rooftop solar uptake under PM Surya Ghar (122.6 MW installed), contrasting with stalled execution and pending PPA terminations in PM-KUSUM Tender-1.
RDSS Phase-IV Fund Claims Pending with REC
BSPTCL Transmission Drone Survey Bids Received

Grid connectivity for ~50k off-grid households in Rohtas, Kaimur, Jamui, and West Champaran is bottlenecked by Stage-1 forest clearances and pending NBWL wildlife approvals within the Valmiki Tiger Reserve.
Substantial grant disbursements (SBPDCL ₹503.23 Cr and NBPDCL ₹292.58 Cr) remain withheld by REC pending qualification in REF evaluations and formal sanction of quantity variations.
Phase-I achieved 100% completion in SBPDCL (59,060 connections) and surpassed targets in NBPDCL (50,784 achieved vs 40,000 target).
Applications surged past 164k across DISCOMs with 34,088 completed installations (75.27 MW in SBPDCL and 47.32 MW in NBPDCL), though 13,078 loan applications remain rejected or unprocessed.
BSPGCL is initiating PPA termination proceedings for 4 non-performing projects (9.7 MW) under Tender-1, while Tender-2 granted extensions up to 23.12.2026 across eligible lagging sites.
Phulwaria Floating Solar (10 MW) reached 87% completion despite DC cable dam crossing issues with WRD, while BERC has reserved orders on the Indrapuri Canal Bank tariff petition.
Geotechnical investigations for the 4x700 MW Banka NPP remain halted due to local resistance pending district police deployment scheduled for 20 November 2026.
Consumer metering reached 55.6% overall deployment led by Secure Meters and Genus, while feeder and DT system metering has achieved virtually 100% installation across both DISCOMs.

Mehta & Mehta CS team has been deployed on-site with PNBISL for readiness due diligence, but procurement of a Project Manager Agency and Virtual Data Room remain pending target closure in October 2026.
The ₹6.85 Cr drone transmission line patrol tender received zero vendor submissions, forcing a 15-day bid extension to 22 October 2026.
Of 3,280 registered complaints, toll-free call centers generated 78.7% of volume, with Muzaffarpur (356), Samastipur (283), and PESU West (245) logging the highest complaint loads.
Kajra Phase-I (185 MW + 254 MWh BESS) is operational post-COD with minor peripheral works remaining, while Phase-II is at 58% physical progress facing site security and module ALMM compliance issues.

Interventions undertaken by the City Accelerator Program

REC & Banks: CAP Team obtained branch-wise loan rejection data from REC and shared it with concerned banks to facilitate resolution of pending loan cases.
High-rejection bank data was shared with the LDM, followed by meetings with concerned banks to reduce loan rejections as directed by the DM and DDC.

Vendor Empanelment: CAP Team guided vendors on the empanelment process and coordinated with DISCOM for smooth and timely onboarding. Regular meetings are conducted with vendors to identify issues and coordinate with DISCOM for timely resolution.

For ULA Consent Mobilization- field visits identified OTP generation and verification issues in the Suvidha App, affecting online consent under the ULA model. The issue was discussed with CMD, BSPHCL, following which Jeevika Didis (SHGs) were onboarded for offline consent collection from Kutir Jyoti/BPL households, accelerating the consent process.

Facilitated Bank Loan Processing: Following sustained intervention in the banking loan process, the loan rejection rate decreased significantly from 49% in February to 28% as of date. The CAP Team facilitated daily review meetings chaired by the DDC with participating banks to address loan-related issues and expedite sanctions and disbursements.

Solar Mela Impact: Introduced Solar Melas in CAP cities(firstly intrroduced by the CAP in the State) to enhance consumer awareness and increase RTS adoption.
Conducted Loan Melas in coordination with Banks, SLBC, District Administrations. The Solar Mela in Muzaffarpur generated 598 rooftop solar applications in single day, equivalent to the district’s average monthly application volume. The success demonstrated the impact of targeted outreach, with subsequent Solar Melas sustaining high application volumes.

Support in Capacity Building Training for Junior Engineers (JEs): Provided support in organizing and facilitating the Capacity Building Training Programme for Junior Engineers (JEs), which was successfully conducted at Patliputra, contributing to strengthening technical knowledge, enhancing operational capabilities, and improving implementation readiness.
CPGRAMS Grievance Resolution: Timely resolved 5 CPGRAMS grievances through close coordination with consumers, DISCOM officials, and REC.
Annual IEC PLAN- In coordination with the DISCOM, finalized by the Energy Secretary, and circulated to all district circles for implementation.

JEEViKA Engagement:
ULA: CAP Team recommended leveraging Jeevika Didis (SHGs) to secure offline consent from BPL households, helping achieve ULA consent targets. 
PMSGY: The CAP team prepared a concept note proposing the engagement of Jeevika Didis in door-to-door awareness and application generation under the PM Surya Ghar scheme, which was subsequently discussed with the Energy Secretary. An MoU has been executed between the DISCOM and JEEViKA to formalize their engagement.

WhatsApp Group for Issue Resolution: A dedicated WhatsApp group comprising vendors, banks, CAP team members, and DISCOM officials has been created to facilitate quick resolution of issues related to loan sanctions, net metering delays, and other RTS installation challenges. Issues are resolved through the group wherever possible, while CAP escalates unresolved matters to the appropriate higher authorities.
